# Cheatsheet

One-page recall card: given what the capture shows, which handler to run and what it gets you. Start here; the full reasoning is in [DETECTIONS.md](DETECTIONS.md) and [decision-guide.md](decision-guide.md).

> Passive analysis only. ACTIVE commands are suggestions; confirm scope.

## Common runs

```bash
pufferrelay -f capture.pcapng --dump out            # everything + agent feed
pufferrelay -f capture.pcapng --credentials-only    # identities/secrets only
pufferrelay -f capture.pcapng --only kerberos,kerberoast,asrepcatcher
pufferrelay -q capture.pcapng --dump out            # add protocol-level weaknesses
pufferrelay -r --has-creds --json                   # ask the database
```

## Passive detections

| Capture looks like | `--only` handler | You get | Watch out |
|---|---|---|---|
| the capture contains an LDAP bindRequest | `ldap` | credentials.csv; users.txt; leads CRED-* | SASL binds expose no password; signing state is not in the packet |
| HTTP requests are present | `http` | credentials.csv, hosts.tsv, leads CRED-* | TLS is opaque; NTLM/SSO authentication is handled by the NTLM handler |
| FTP control traffic is present | `ftp` | credentials.csv; leads CRED-* | FTPS is opaque; binary payloads are not part of the credential row |
| Telnet negotiation or data is present | `telnet` | credentials.csv; leads CRED-* | heuristic; a prompt without a completed login is not a credential |
| SMTP authentication is present | `smtp` | credentials.csv; leads CRED-* | TLS submission is opaque; OAuth flows expose no password |
| IMAP LOGIN or AUTHENTICATE is present | `imap` | credentials.csv; leads CRED-* | tshark truncates imap.request.password; AUTHENTICATE may expose only the identity |
| POP3 USER/PASS or APOP is present | `pop3` | credentials.csv; leads CRED-* | STLS is opaque; APOP exposes a digest, not the password |
| NTLMSSP messages or HTTP NTLM headers are present | `ntlm` | ntlm-hashes.txt; leads HASH-* | relay feasibility depends on the destination's signing policy (see relays) |
| NBNS name/registration frames are present | `netbios` | hosts.tsv; leads QW/NETBIOS when anomalous | names are self-asserted; no proof the host still exists |
| SNMP v1/v2c traffic is present | `snmp` | credentials.csv; quick win SNMPv1/SNMPv2 | SNMPv3 auth/priv is not parsed |
| AS-REQ/AS-REP exchanges are present | `kerberos` | asrep-hashes.txt; leads ASREP-* | an encrypted AS-REP is not a cracked password; Kerberoasting is separate |
| NTLM authentication crosses SMB, LDAP or HTTP and the destination signing state is visible | `relays` | relay-targets.txt, relays.tsv; leads RELAY-* | the capture does not prove a relay was attempted or will succeed |
| SMB tree connects, creates or reads are present | `smb` | smb-shares.txt, smb-files.txt; leads SMB-*, SMBFILE-* | file names come from CREATE/READ frames; content needs smbobjects |
| HTTP responses or FTP-DATA carry file objects | `files` | files.tsv, files/; leads FILE-* | 1 MiB/object, 16 MiB/capture; TLS and segmented SMB are opaque |
| EAPOL/EAP or RADIUS frames are present | `nac` | nac.txt; leads NAC-* | no keys; spoof proposals are Tier B and not generated here |
| HTTP requests look like Windows Update/WSUS | `wsus` | wsus.txt; leads WSUS-* | approval state and package integrity are not visible |
| TCP SYN/acknowledgement traffic is present | `services` | hosts.tsv, nmap-targets.txt | only observed ports; no banner or version unless another handler sees it |
| IP traffic is present | `ips` | ips.txt, subnets.txt | a capture from a tap may include unrelated hosts |
| DNS queries/answers are present | `dns` | dns.txt; hostnames in hosts.tsv | one answer per row when a response carries several records; DoH/DoT is opaque |
| Kerberos and ARP frames can be correlated | `asrepcatcher` | asrepcatcher.txt; leads ASREPCATCHER-*; console panel with the repo link | heuristic; a partial capture cannot correlate a reply; not proof of intent |
| TGS-REQ/TGS-REP exchanges are present | `kerberoast` | kerberoast-hashes.txt; leads KERBEROAST-*, KERBEROASTCAND-* | fragmented/unreassembled DER yields a candidate without a hash; SPN-to-account resolution needs directory data |
| HTTP requests/responses carry authentication headers, cookies or token-shaped strings | `httptokens` | tokens.tsv (fingerprints); leads TOKEN-* | TLS is opaque; headers split across TCP segments may be missed; JWT signature is not verified |
| DCE/RPC binds/requests to EFSRPC, RPRN, DFSNM or FSRVP are present | `coercion` | coercions.tsv; leads COERCE-* | encrypted RPC is opaque; a bind or pipe without a UNC path is normal traffic and is ignored |
| HTTP /certsrv enrollment or Kerberos PKINIT is present | `adcs` | adcs.tsv; leads ADCS-* | template attributes are usually not visible; DCOM-only enrollment is not fully parsed |
| DHCPv6, ICMPv6 router advertisements or DNS UPDATE are present | `ipv6` | ipv6.tsv; leads IPV6-* | no baseline of the legitimate resolver; confirm before calling it rogue |
| Redis, MySQL or PostgreSQL traffic is present | `dbcreds` | db-creds.tsv; leads DB-* | MSSQL stays with the NTLM handler; SCRAM/native responses need the matching hashcat mode |
| SMB traffic carries file objects that tshark can reassemble | `smbobjects` | files.tsv, files/ | 8 MiB/object, 16 MiB/capture; SMB3 encryption and missing reassembly yield nothing |
| SCCM management/distribution HTTP or SMS shares are present | `sccm` | sccm.tsv; leads SCCM-* | SMS Provider DCOM and policy objects are not parsed; package delivery alone is inventory |
| HTTP traffic targets an LLM service, MCP endpoint or vector database | `llm` | llm.tsv; leads LLM-* | TLS is opaque; ambiguous ports are recognised only by path markers; prompts are not exported |
| -q is used, or -f is combined with -q | `quickwins` | quick_wins table; leads QW-* | presence is not exploitability; signing may be enforced elsewhere |

## Active modes (opt-in, warned, authorized)

| Need | Mode | Guard rail |
|---|---|---|
| no capture exists yet and you can capture on an authorized interface | `--live` | requires --live, --bpf and --duration; red warning and authorization; temp file deleted unless kept |
| you need to observe one TCP target through a local relay | `--proxy` | one target, bounded duration, explicit warning and authorization |
| the inventory suggests an ARP/relay path and you want reviewable commands | `--commands` | text only; every line is ACTIVE and includes cleanup |
| you want a next-step command per host or finding | `--serveme` | text only; ACTIVE lines are marked |

## Triage order

1. `services` + `ips` + `dns` — know the battlefield.
2. `httptokens`, `ldap`, `http`, `ftp`, `smtp`, `imap`, `pop3`, `snmp`,
   `dbcreds` — reusable secrets first.
3. `kerberos`, `kerberoast`, `ntlm`, `asrepcatcher` — offline-crackable material.
4. `relays`, `coercion`, `adcs`, `sccm`, `ipv6`, `smb` — attack paths.
5. `files`, `smbobjects` — content that decides the engagement.
